language.script_notes: German/Scandinavian-derived town names common (Minnesota, Wisconsin, the Dakotas) reflecting 19th-century immigration.

road_furniture.line_paint: Roads follow an extremely regular section-line grid (a legacy of the Public Land Survey System) — long dead-straight rural roads meeting at right angles are a very strong Midwest/Great Plains tell.
road_furniture.curb_style: Open roadside ditches in rural farmland; curbed streets in towns.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Grain elevators (tall concrete/steel cylindrical silos) visible on the horizon near small towns are a near-unique Midwest tell.

architecture.roof_style: Simple gable roofs on farmhouses; distinctive round and octagonal barns were historically most popular in this region (1880s-1920s).
architecture.wall_construction: Wood-frame farmhouses; red brick common in older industrial Rust Belt cities (Chicago, Detroit, Cleveland); classic red 'Midwest Three-Portal' gambrel barns beside farmhouses.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White farmhouses with red barns is the classic regional palette; red brick in older industrial city cores.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Red gambrel/round barns beside white farmhouses; grain elevators; small-town Main Streets with brick storefronts; Rust Belt industrial architecture in Great Lakes cities.

nature.vegetation: Vast flat corn and soybean cropland (the 'Corn Belt') dominates the landscape; treeless wheat prairie further west on the Great Plains; scattered woodlots and windbreak tree lines between fields.
nature.terrain: Famously flat to gently rolling — glaciated plains around the Great Lakes, flattening into the true high plains toward the Dakotas/Nebraska/Kansas; the Great Lakes themselves visible as huge inland water bodies.
nature.climate_signature: Wide-open big-sky horizons over flat farmland; harsh snowy winters, green humid summers; frequent long straight-road vanishing-point shots.

vehicles.plate_color: Varies by state — Illinois blue-on-white, Ohio blue-and-white with a state outline, Michigan blue-and-white, Minnesota blue-and-white with loon imagery.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Farm equipment (tractors, combines) visible in season; pickup trucks common; otherwise standard national fleet.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations; dense modern coverage around Chicago and other major cities, older/thinner in remote Great Plains counties.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very complete grid coverage of rural section-line roads is a hallmark of this region — Street View literally follows the farm grid for miles.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat farmland, grain elevators, similar grid road layout, similar climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: US plates carry a state name and yellow center lines with mph signage; Canadian prairie provinces use km/h signage and provincial plates, and Canadian grain elevators/architecture carry subtly different branding and styles.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Rural farmland, wood-frame houses, similar road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Midwest is flatter with a rigid section-line grid and corn/soy cropland; the South has red clay, pine forest, kudzu and a hazier, more humid look with less rigid road grids.
